message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever house rule you set). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno deck).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining deck face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. If it’s a special card, apply its effect immediately. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a reverse card is played). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card that matches either the **color** or the **number/symbol** of the top discard.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses direction of play.
• **Draw Two (+2)** – Next player draws two cards and skips their turn.
• **Wild** – You choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four (+4)** – You choose the new color and the next player draws four cards. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise you risk a challenge.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you play your second‑to‑last card, shout “UNO!” before the next player starts their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of the cards left in opponents’ hands:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points.
• Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points. | | **Game End** | First player to reach the target score (usually 500) wins the game. | --- ### Quick Tips 1. **Keep track of the current color** – Even if you’re holding a Wild, you still need to match the color if possible. 2. **Use Draw Two/Draw Four strategically** – Save them for when you’re about to win or when you’re in a tight spot. 3. **Watch for “UNO” calls** – It’s easy to forget, but missing it costs you two cards. 4. **Challenge a Wild Draw Four** – If you suspect the previous player had a playable card, you can challenge. If they were right, you draw four; if they were wrong, you draw six. Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
